introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$\mathbf{r} = [(2\sin 2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (1-\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{j}]\ \mathrm{m}.$$

Find
incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total de points par question ; l'énoncé dit seulement « All questions carry equal marks ». Les points imprimés par partie somment à 13 pour chacune des 8 questions (total 104) ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide (sauf la question 5, dont le total de 13 points est imprimé).
Le scan compte 3 pages (page de garde, puis les questions 1 à 6 et les questions 7 et 8) : les 8 questions sont présentes, rien ne manque. Filigranes et publicités de gcerevision.com ignorés.

Question 1 : l'énoncé imprimé contient deux fautes de frappe (« positon », « kinetic ernegy »), corrigées en « position » et « kinetic energy » dans la transcription. Les unités de r sont des mètres (« m » imprimé).

questions.enonce_markdown: the velocity and the acceleration of the particle when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method.** Velocity is the derivative of the position vector with respect to time and acceleration is the derivative of the velocity.

$$\mathbf{v} = \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{dt} = (4\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (2\sin 2t)\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

$$\mathbf{a} = \frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt} = (-8\sin 2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (4\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ we have $2t = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, with $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac12$ and $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$$\mathbf{v} = 4\left(\tfrac12\right)\mathbf{i} + 2\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\mathbf{j} = (2\mathbf{i} + \sqrt3\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

$$\mathbf{a} = -8\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\mathbf{i} + 4\left(\tfrac12\right)\mathbf{j} = (-4\sqrt3\,\mathbf{i} + 2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

Magnitudes: $|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{4 + 3} = \sqrt7 \approx 2.65\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, at about $40.9^\circ$ above the direction of $\mathbf{i}$. $|\mathbf{a}| = \sqrt{48 + 4} = 2\sqrt{13} \approx 7.21\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, at about $163.9^\circ$ from the direction of $\mathbf{i}$.

**Velocity $= (2\mathbf{i} + \sqrt3\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and acceleration $= (-4\sqrt3\,\mathbf{i} + 2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the kinetic energy of the particle when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
The kinetic energy is $\tfrac12 m|\mathbf{v}|^2$ with $m = 2\ \mathrm{kg}$ and, from part (a), $|\mathbf{v}|^2 = 2^2 + (\sqrt3)^2 = 7\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$.

$$E_k = \tfrac12 (2)(7) = 7\ \mathrm{J}$$

**Kinetic energy $= 7\ \mathrm{J}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the force acting on the particle when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
By Newton's second law the (resultant) force is $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}$ with $m = 2\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathbf{a}$ from part (a).

$$\mathbf{F} = 2\,(-4\sqrt3\,\mathbf{i} + 2\,\mathbf{j}) = (-8\sqrt3\,\mathbf{i} + 4\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N} \approx (-13.9\,\mathbf{i} + 4\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N}$$

Its magnitude is $|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{192 + 16} = \sqrt{208} = 4\sqrt{13} \approx 14.4\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Force $= (-8\sqrt3\,\mathbf{i} + 4\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N}$, of magnitude $4\sqrt{13} \approx 14.4\ \mathrm{N}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the values of $t$ where $0 \le t \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for which the velocity of the particle is perpendicular to its acceleration.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when their scalar product is zero.

$$\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a} = (4\cos 2t)(-8\sin 2t) + (2\sin 2t)(4\cos 2t) = -32\sin 2t\cos 2t + 8\sin 2t\cos 2t = -24\sin 2t\cos 2t$$

Using $\sin 4t = 2\sin 2t\cos 2t$:

$$\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{a} = -12\sin 4t = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \sin 4t = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 4t = n\pi$$

For $0 \le t \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ we need $0 \le 4t \le 2\pi$, so $4t = 0,\ \pi,\ 2\pi$, that is $t = 0,\ \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

**Neither vector is ever zero**, so these are genuine right angles: $|\mathbf{v}|^2 = 16\cos^2 2t + 4\sin^2 2t \ge 4$ and $|\mathbf{a}|^2 = 64\sin^2 2t + 16\cos^2 2t \ge 16$.

Check:
- $t = 0$: $\mathbf{v} = 4\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{a} = 4\mathbf{j}$ (perpendicular);
- $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $\mathbf{v} = 2\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{a} = -8\mathbf{i}$ (perpendicular);
- $t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$: $\mathbf{v} = -4\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{a} = -4\mathbf{j}$ (perpendicular).

**The velocity is perpendicular to the acceleration at $t = 0,\ \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ seconds.**
